convertedTask.title: AWS Database Migration Service (DMS) Conceptual Guide
convertedTask.goal: Goal: Step-by-step walkthrough detailing DMS Replication Instances, Source/Target Endpoints, and CDC (Change Data Capture) configuration for minimal downtime migrations.

concepts.title: AWS DMS Replication Instance
concepts.body: Managed EC2 instance running AWS DMS migration software that connects to source/target endpoints, extracts data, and loads records.

concepts.title: DMS Endpoints
concepts.body: Connection definitions holding IP address, port, engine type, and credentials for source and target databases.

concepts.title: Full Load + CDC (Change Data Capture)
concepts.body: Full Load migrates existing table records. CDC continuously streams ongoing binary log changes until application cutover.

concepts.title: Homogeneous vs Heterogeneous
concepts.body: DMS natively migrates homogeneous databases (e.g. MySQL to RDS MySQL). Heterogeneous migrations (e.g. Oracle to Aurora) require AWS SCT for schema conversion.

concepts.title: DMS Migration Architecture Plan
concepts.body: DMS ComponentFunctionKey RequirementReplication InstanceExecutes data extraction & loadingNeeds network connectivity to source & targetSource EndpointReads source database records & binlogsRequires binlog/CDC privileges on source DBTarget EndpointWrites records to destination DBRequires target schema tables pre-createdMigration TaskDefines task type & table mapping rulesSelect Full Load + CDC for minimal downtime

convertedTask.whyItMatters: This matters because continuous database replication with minimal application downtime is a major scenario topic on SAA-C03.
convertedTask.costWarning: Architectural Guide: Reading this conceptual guide incurs $0 cost.

consoleSteps.title: Review AWS DMS Administration Permissions

instructions.text: Ensure your identity has permissions for DMS replication instances and endpoints.

consoleSteps.note: Read-only access is sufficient for evaluation.

consoleSteps.title: Provision DMS Replication Instance and Endpoints

instructions.text: Open Database Migration Service (DMS) Console.
Provision a DMS Replication Instance (e.g. dms.t3.micro).
Configure Source Database Endpoint with source DB IP, port, and credentials.
Configure Target Database Endpoint pointing to Amazon RDS or Aurora.
Choose Test connection to verify network connectivity between endpoints.

consoleSteps.note: Sets up the core DMS replication infrastructure.

consoleSteps.title: Configure and Execute Full Load + CDC Migration Task

instructions.text: Create a Migration Task selecting Full load + CDC (Change Data Capture).
Configure Table Mapping selection rules (Schema %, Table %).
Start task and monitor initial Full Load completion.
Monitor continuous CDC binary log replication until replication latency reaches 0 seconds.

consoleSteps.note: Enables initial data snapshot followed by continuous change streaming.

consoleSteps.title: Perform Zero-Downtime Application Cutover

instructions.text: Redirect application traffic to target database.
Stop and delete the DMS task and replication instance.

consoleSteps.warning: Delete the replication instance after cutover to stop hourly charges.

cliSteps.note: Expected: account ID and IAM user/role ARN.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Expected: account ID and IAM user/role ARN.

cheatSheet.title: AWS DMS
cheatSheet.body: Migrates databases to AWS with minimal downtime. Supports relational, NoSQL, and data warehouse targets.

cheatSheet.title: Change Data Capture (CDC)
cheatSheet.body: Continuously streams ongoing binlog modifications to target database during migration.

cheatSheet.title: Homogeneous vs Heterogeneous
cheatSheet.body: Homogeneous migrations use DMS alone. Heterogeneous migrations require AWS SCT for schema conversion first.

troubleshooting.title: CDC Replication Failing on Source
troubleshooting.body: Ensure binary logging (`binlog_format=ROW`) is enabled on the source database and DMS user has replication privileges.

examTraps.title: DMS Schema Conversion Trap
examTraps.body: AWS DMS does NOT convert database schemas between different engines. You MUST use AWS SCT to convert schema before running DMS.

examTips.text: SAA-C03: Master Amazon RDS concepts and multi-AZ / replication design in Amazon RDS.

convertedTask.title: Homogeneous vs Heterogeneous Database Migration
convertedTask.goal: Goal: Operational workflow comparing same-engine migrations (DMS alone) vs. engine changes (Oracle/SQL Server to Postgres/Aurora requiring AWS Schema Conversion Tool).

concepts.title: Homogeneous Migration
concepts.body: Source and target database engines are identical (e.g. MySQL to RDS MySQL, Oracle to RDS Oracle). Schemas match natively; AWS SCT is NOT required.

concepts.title: Heterogeneous Migration
concepts.body: Source and target database engines are different (e.g. Oracle to Aurora PostgreSQL, SQL Server to MySQL). Schemas and SQL dialects MUST be converted using AWS SCT.

concepts.title: AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT)
concepts.body: Converts source database schemas, views, indexes, stored procedures, and DDL statements into the target engine dialect automatically.

concepts.title: SCT Assessment Report
concepts.body: Generates a detailed report identifying code items that require manual conversion assistance (e.g., complex stored procedures or proprietary functions).

concepts.title: Homogeneous vs Heterogeneous Decision Matrix
concepts.body: FeatureHomogeneous MigrationHeterogeneous MigrationEngine alignmentSame source and target (e.g. Postgres -> RDS Postgres)Different source and target (e.g. SQL Server -> Aurora)Schema tool needed?No (Schemas match natively)YES — AWS SCT RequiredData migration toolAWS DMS or native backup tools (`pg_dump`/`mysqldump`)AWS DMS (Data migration after SCT schema conversion)Stored procedure conversionAutomatic (Identical dialect)AWS SCT converts or flags for manual review

convertedTask.whyItMatters: This matters because knowing exactly when AWS SCT is required alongside AWS DMS is a classic SAA-C03 exam scenario.

consoleSteps.title: Review AWS DMS and AWS SCT Administration Permissions

instructions.text: Ensure your identity has permissions to manage DMS resources.

consoleSteps.note: Read-only access is sufficient for evaluation.

consoleSteps.title: Evaluate Homogeneous Migration Path (DMS Alone)

instructions.text: Select Homogeneous Migration when source and target database engines are identical (e.g. MySQL to RDS MySQL).
Use native database tools (`mysqldump`, `pg_dump`) or AWS DMS alone.
Note that AWS SCT is NOT required for homogeneous migrations.

consoleSteps.note: Schemas match natively across identical engines.

consoleSteps.title: Evaluate Heterogeneous Migration Path (AWS SCT + DMS)

instructions.text: Select Heterogeneous Migration when source and target database engines differ (e.g. Oracle to Aurora PostgreSQL).
Download and launch AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT).
Connect SCT to Source DB and Target RDS DB.
Generate SCT Schema Transformation Assessment Report.
Convert DDL statements, tables, views, and stored procedures to target dialect.
Apply converted schema to target database.
Run AWS DMS to migrate data records into target schema.

consoleSteps.note: SCT converts schema first; DMS migrates data records after.

instructions.text: Verify your tool choice: SCT for schema conversion; DMS for data migration.

cheatSheet.title: Homogeneous Migration
cheatSheet.body: Same engine (e.g. MySQL to RDS MySQL). Schemas match. AWS SCT is NOT required; use DMS alone.

cheatSheet.title: Heterogeneous Migration
cheatSheet.body: Different engine (e.g. Oracle to Aurora Postgres). MUST use **AWS SCT** for schema conversion before running **AWS DMS** for data.

cheatSheet.title: AWS SCT
cheatSheet.body: Converts source schema DDL, views, indexes, and stored procedures to target database engine dialect.

troubleshooting.title: Target Table Missing for DMS
troubleshooting.body: DMS does not create complex schemas for heterogeneous migrations. Run AWS SCT first to create target tables before starting DMS.

examTraps.title: AWS SCT for Homogeneous Trap
examTraps.body: If an exam question describes a homogeneous migration (e.g. PostgreSQL to RDS PostgreSQL), do NOT select AWS SCT. SCT is only for heterogeneous migrations.
